Reported Spill Volume: 105 gallon
Report Description/// UPDATE TO INCIDENT REPORT # 1384511 /// /// NEEC INCIDENT NOTIFICATION /// UPDATE: RECEIVED ON 2023-11-16 22:03 ET | CALLER REPORTS THAT A SUNBURY TRACTOR-TRAILER FELL OFF THE BRIDGE (THE CAUSE IS UNKNOWN), DOWN 1600 FEET, ENDING UP 45 DEGREES ON THE EMBANKMENT, HANGING OVER DENNIS STREAM, WITH THE RADIATOR IN THE STREAM. BOTH SADDLE TANKS OF THE TRUCK ARE COMPLETELY EMPTY, DICTATING THAT 350 L – 400 L OF DIESEL HAS SPILLED UNTO THE EMBANKMENT AND VERY LIKELY INTO THE STREAM. CALLER EXPLAINS THAT THE EMBANKMENT IS CONSTRUCTED WITH SHALE ROCK (LARGE AND LOOSE ROCKS USED TO BUILD HIGHWAYS), AND THERE IS NO MORE DIESEL ODOR AT THE SITE OF THE ACCIDENT. SEEING IT IS DARK OUTSIDE, THE SPILL IS NOT VISIBLE, BUT IT IS VERY LIKELY THAT THE DIESEL SPILLED INTO THE STREAM. THE TRUCK WAS CARRYING CORRUGATED CARDBOARD. CALLER INDICATES THAT THE CALL WAS RECEIVED ON 2023-11-16 AT 19:51. ACCORDING TO SUNBURY, THE TRUCK’S COMPUTER TRACKING SYSTEM INDICATES THAT THE TRUCK CAME TO A STOP ON 2023-11-16 AT 18H58. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CAME AND PINCHED THE FUEL LINE, AND SOME ABSORBENT PADS ARE BEING PLACED. BOTH THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND THE POLICE HAVE LEFT. A RIVER BOOM WILL BE BROUGHT IN TO CATCH ANY REMNANT DIESEL. AT THIS POINT, IT IS UNKNOWN WHERE THE DIESEL HAS SPILLED. RST EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND THE INSURANCE ARE ON SITE. CALLER EXPLAINS THAT RST EMERGENCY RESPONSE IS A HAZMAT RESPONSE TEAM FROM TRANSPORT CANADA AND IS A SISTER COMPANY TO SUNBURY. BOTH COMPANIES ARE UNDER THE UMBRELLA OF IRVING OIL.

WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK ON NOVEMBER 22, 2010 (ALONG THE REVETMENT), SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708).

properties.content:
Report Details

Nearest City: Dawsonville, GA

Incident Type: FIXED
Material: HYDROGEN PEROXIDE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: BTD MANUFACTURING
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 34.358629, -84.053249 (Approximated from premise)
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS THAT SOMETIME BETWEEN THE PM OF 26TH AND 27TH OF MAY, A TWO-INCH PIPING ON THE FILTER HOUSING AT A METAL PROCESSING FACILITY BURST WHICH WAS CONNECTED TO A STORAGE TANK. THE TANK CONTAINED A PRIMER WITH THE FOLLOWING MATERIALS (BY PERCENTAGE): 85% REVERSE OSMOSIS WATER 12% MPP930 2% HYDROGEN PEROXIDE 1% HYDROGEN FLUORIDE APPROXIMATELY 2200 TOTAL GALLONS RELEASED. MOST OF THE MATERIAL WENT INTO SECONDARY CONTAINMENT, BUT THE BURST PIPING ALSO SPRAYED SOME MATERIAL INTO A STORM DRAIN THAT LED INTO A RETENTION POND. RAIN CONDITIONS ON THE POND LED SOME MATERIAL (POSSIBLY 130 GALLONS) TO RELEASE ONTO THE ADJACENT PROPERTY, INTO AN UNNAMED STREAM, AND THEN INTO BRUCE LAKE. THE FACILITY WAS CLOSED AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT AND WAS DISCOVERED ON THE 27TH.

IT HAD AN UNNATURAL, SEGMENTED SHAPE WITH LIGHT FEATHERING VISIBLE IN CERTAIN SECTIONS. IT MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 4.70 NM IN LENGTH AND 0.98 NM AT ITS WIDEST POINT. ADDITIONALLY, IT WAS OBSERVED14.53 NM NORTHEAST OF THE ANOMALY REPORTED IN NOAA/NESDIS NRC REPORT #1466720 (7/1), BUT ANY CONNECTION BETWEEN THE TWO WAS UNCERTAIN.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 43.896944, -69.809444 (Explicit)
Report DescriptionAMPLIFYING INFORMATION: - USCG SECTOR NORTHER NEW ENGLAND RECEIVED A NOTIFICATION FROM SEA TOW THAT THE MAINE MARITIME MUSEUM SAILING VESSEL (S/V) MARY E WITH 15 PASSENGERS AND 3 CREW MEMBERS WAS SINKING IN THE KENNEBEK RIVER NEAR DOUBLING POINT. - THE VESSEL WAS KNOCKED DOWN BIG A LARGE GUST OF WIND, CAPSIZED AND WAS UNABLE TO RIGHT ITSELF. - SECTOR NORTHER NEW ENGLAND ISSUED AN UMIB, LAUNCHED STATION BOOTHBAY HARBOR AND REQUESTED AIR SUPPORT FROM AIR STATION CAPE COD. - PRIOR TO CG ASSETS ARRIVING, SEA TOW AND BATH COUNTY FIRE RESPONDED, ARRIVED ON SCENE AND RESCUED AND ACCOUNTED FOR ALL 15 PASSENGERS AND 3 CREW MEMBERS. - 2 PASSENGERS RECEIVED EMS TREATMENT AND WERE TRANSFERRED TO MIDCOAST HOSPITAL: 1 ELDERLY FEMALE FOR POSSIBLE FRACTURES AND 1 ELDERLY MALE FOR HYPOTHERMIA. - MARINE PATROL UNITS ARE ON SCENE AND THE VESSEL HAS BEEN REPORTED AS A COMPLETE LOSS. - SECTOR NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND INVESTIGATIVE OFFICERS AND MARINE INSPECTORS HAVE BEEN NOTIFIED AND AND RESPONDING TO INVESTIGATE AND QUERY THE CREW AND PASSENGERS - THE VESSEL SANK WITH THE STERN AND STARBOARD QUARTER STICKING UP. - SECTOR NORTHER NEW ENGLAND ISSUED A SAFETY MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST AND ESTABLISHED A SAFETY ZONE. - THERE CURRENTLY NO SIGNIFICANT MEDIA ATTENTION. - THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN.

CALLER RENTS THE PROPERTY AND WAS TOLD THE TANK WAS EMPTY BEFORE MOVING IN. A GAUGE ON TOP OF THE TANK ALSO SHOWS IT BEING EMPTY. CALLER IS REPORTING A MATERIAL RELEASE DISCOVERY FROM A HOME HEATING OIL TANK LOCATED INSIDE HIS BASEMENT THAT IS NO LONGER IN USE. CALLER RENTS THE PROPERTY AND WAS TOLD THE TANK WAS EMPTY BEFORE MOVING IN. A GAUGE ON TOP OF THE TANK ALSO SHOWS IT BEING EMPTY. APPARENTLY THE TANK WAS FULL AND RECENTLY SPRUNG A LEAK RELEASING MATERIAL INTO THE FLOOR DRAIN. CALLER STATES FIRE DEPT RESPONDED AND MOPPED UP THE MATERIAL. PUTTY WAS PUT ON THE TANK TO STOP THE LEAK BUT THAT DID NOT SEEM TO WORK. A SLOW LEAK IS STILL ONGOING. THERE IS AN ADDITIONAL TANK CONNECTED TO THE ONE THAT IS LEAKING BUT NOTHING HAS SEEM TO LEAK OUT OF IT AT THIS TIME.

UNCERTAINTIES: THERE WERE MULTIPLE OIL FACILITIES NEAR THE SLICK SO IT IS POSSIBLE THE SICK WAS ASSOCIATED WITH A DIFFERENT PLATFORM.
